# ToolPrune: hierarchical tool retrieval

Context brief for coding agents. Read this first. Detailed planning happens in follow-up tasks.

## What we are building

A training-free tool retriever. An LLM enriches each MCP/API tool with facet annotations, then queries are routed by pruning hierarchically (L0 function family, then L1 domain, then tool), so the agent sees only the few tools it needs.

Example: `search_1` (image search) sits under L1 `image` and `search_2` (contact lookup) under L1 `contact info`, both under L0 `search_tools`. A query about photos never reaches `search_2`.

**Hypothesis (unproven):** on queries where tool names or descriptions collide, hierarchical routing over enriched annotations makes fewer confusion errors than embedding search, and uses far fewer context tokens. We must measure this, not assume it. Most of the gain may come from the enrichment alone, not the hierarchy.

- All code is written during the event. Public repo, commits dated Oct 10 to 12.

# Counterparty Pre-check: neatHack Plan

Oct 10, 2026

## Summary

We are building an agent that pre-checks a prospective business counterparty in India (company, LLP or proprietor) from public sources and returns a cited, confidence-rated report. Working name is still open.

- **User:** a small business deciding whether to give credit to, or work with, a vendor, customer or partner of a similar size.
- **Input:** a name, plus any identifiers on hand (CIN, GSTIN, PAN, city).
- **Output:** a schema-validated report where every claim links to its evidence, plus a list of what could not be verified.
- **Built in 48 hours:** the pre-check only.
- **Not built:** the post-check (needs the counterparty's consent and guarded sources), default prediction, personal dossiers on individuals, LinkedIn scraping.
- **Moat direction, not yet real:** affordable, explainable reports for tiny businesses, and later a feedback loop from actual payment outcomes.
- **Why it fits the rubric:** a multi-step agent (resolve the entity, gather signals, reconcile conflicts, verify claims, report) with failure recovery and verification built in.

## Rules and rubric

The agent is 30% of the score, and all three sponsor tools must be used and shown in the demo. Source: [neatHack page](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon), read on Oct 10, 2026. Re-check it before submitting.

- **Dates (IST):** build Oct 10 (starts 12:30 PM) to Oct 12; submissions Oct 12, 7:00 to 11:55 PM; winners Oct 16.
- **One track:** build an agent that completes a substantial task start to finish. Judged areas include planning, tool use, state, context, execution, recovery, verification and iteration.
- **Required tools:** neatlogs and Entire to build and improve the agent; cfo.ai to plan its business (pricing, costs, revenue, runway), with the plan included in the submission.
- **Demo video, 3 minutes max:** must explicitly cover architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning and result for each of the three tools.
- **Submit:** public repo with commits dated during the event, plus a quote post of the official neatlogs post on X.

| Category | Weight | What judges look at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The agent | 30% | How well it handles a substantial task end to end |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | How well each was used to build, improve and plan the business |
| Demo video | 20% | Clarity of the agent and of the use of all three tools |
| Building in public | 15% | What we shared while building, tagged #neatHack |
| Usefulness and originality | 10% | A real problem, solved in a new way |

Evidence the submission must carry:

- [ ] Two neatlogs traces, before and after a change, with the numbers compared
- [ ] A neatlogs run where an action failed and the agent recovered
- [ ] Entire checkpoints or entire-graph output from our repo
- [ ] A cfo.ai business plan: pricing, costs, revenue, runway
- [ ] Links to build-in-public posts tagged #neatHack
- [ ] Public repo with commits dated Oct 10 to 12

Credits and setup: AWS credits go to the first 200 teams to complete web check-in; Crustdata gives 5,000 credits to everyone. For cfo.ai, sign up at cfo.ai/neathacks; the page says a card is required and the subscription must be cancelled right away in Settings, then Billing, and the organizers supply the credits.

## Sources to build connectors for

Six sources cover companies and LLPs; proprietors get a thinner report. Everything below was checked through search results only, not by opening each source, so open each one in the first hours of the build.

| Source | What it gives | Lookup key | Access | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Identifier checks (offline) | Format and checksum validity of PAN, GSTIN, CIN; entity type decoded from the PAN | PAN, GSTIN, CIN | None needed | From our own knowledge of the formats; confirm while building |
| [MCA company master on data.gov.in](https://data.gov.in/catalog/company-master-data) | Status, registration date, capital, class, registered office, industry code for about 3.67M companies | CIN or name | Personal data.gov.in API key | No directors, DIN, charges or AGM dates. License not considered open by one open-data index, so read the terms. LLP coverage unconfirmed |
| [IBBI public announcements](https://www.ibbi.gov.in/public-announcement) | Insolvency and liquidation process announcements, listed with the company CIN | CIN | Public website; check its terms, cache snapshots | Pages keyed by CIN seen in search results |
| GST taxpayer status | Status, constitution, registration date, business activity | GSTIN | Portal search is captcha-gated with no public third-party API; use a licensed provider (one advertises 10 free lookups, untested) or fixtures | We will not use captcha-solving tools |
| Adverse media | News and public reports that mention the entity | Name plus city | Web search tool | Lowest confidence; every claim needs a cited link |
| Crustdata (optional) | Company and people data APIs | Name or domain | 5,000 credits for all participants | Coverage of small Indian businesses unknown; test on 5 entities in hour 1, drop if thin |

**Dropped or deferred:** LinkedIn (personal data and terms-of-use problems), eCourts (captcha-gated, no open API verified, shown as roadmap), director-level data, Udyam.

**Proprietors:** they have no MCA record, so the report rests on GST, identifier checks and media only. The report must say so, with lower confidence. That graceful degradation is a feature to demo.

## Architecture

A plain state machine: each step is a function with its own neatlogs span, so failures and retries show per step, and the verifier is what makes the report trustworthy.

```
Name + identifiers          (CIN, GSTIN, PAN, city)
  -> Validate identifiers   (checksum, entity type)
  -> Resolve entity         (prune MCA candidates)
  -> Connectors, run in parallel (a failed one is marked unverified)
       MCA master | IBBI | GST status | Adverse media
  -> Reconcile              (rank source trust)
  -> Synthesize             (risk bands)
  -> Verify                 (every claim cited)
       uncited claim: fix or drop -> back to Synthesize
  -> Report                 (with confidence)
```

Identifiers are validated first, the entity is resolved against MCA candidates, connectors run in parallel, conflicts are reconciled, and the verifier drops or fixes any claim that lacks a cited signal.

**Signal record, returned by every connector:** source, signal type, value, observed date, evidence URL, source confidence, match confidence.

**Where pruning is used:** entity resolution narrows MCA candidates by name, state, address and age before any model judgment, so the model sees a handful of candidates, not millions.

**Stack:** Python 3.12 with uv, Pydantic, httpx, a SQLite cache of raw responses, Streamlit, the Anthropic SDK (a small model for resolution, a stronger one for the explanation), and the neatlogs workflow `counterparty-precheck`.

## Eval plan

The eval measures whether the agent finds the right entity, extracts the right signals and backs every claim with a source. It does not measure whether a counterparty will default, and we must not claim it does. Ground truth comes from the same public sources the agent reads, so a good score proves resolution, extraction and citation quality, not risk judgment.

| Test group | Count | Ground truth from | What it tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Healthy active companies | 15 | MCA status | False-alarm rate |
| Under insolvency or liquidation | 10 | IBBI announcement, matched by CIN | Signal recall |
| Struck-off companies | 5 | MCA status field | Status recall |

## Summary

We are building an agent that pre-checks a prospective business counterparty in India (company, LLP or proprietor) from public sources and returns a cited, confidence-rated report. Working name is still open.

- **User:** a small business deciding whether to give credit to, or work with, a vendor, customer or partner of a similar size.
- **Input:** a name, plus any identifiers on hand (CIN, GSTIN, PAN, city).
- **Output:** a schema-validated report where every claim links to its evidence, plus a list of what could not be verified.
- **Built in 48 hours:** the pre-check only.
- **Not built:** the post-check (needs the counterparty's consent and guarded sources), default prediction, personal dossiers on individuals, LinkedIn scraping.
- **Moat direction, not yet real:** affordable, explainable reports for tiny businesses, and later a feedback loop from actual payment outcomes.

The agent is 30% of the score, and all three sponsor tools must be used and shown in the demo. Source: [neatHack page](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon), read on Oct 10, 2026. Re-check it before submitting.

A plain state machine: each step is a function with its own neatlogs span, so failures and retries show per step, and the verifier is what makes the report trustworthy.

  -> Synthesize             (risk bands)
  -> Verify                 (every claim cited)

  -> Report                 (with confidence)

"""Scrape LiveMCPBench raw files from Hugging Face into data/raw and record a manifest."""

import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

BASE = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/ICIP/LiveMCPBench/resolve/main"
FILES = {
    "tools.json": f"{BASE}/tools/tools.json",
    "all_config.json": f"{BASE}/tools/all_config.json",
    "tasks.json": f"{BASE}/tasks/tasks.json",
}


def fetch_raw(raw_dir: Path, force: bool = False) -> dict:
    raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    manifest = {}
    with httpx.Client(follow_redirects=True, timeout=120) as client:
        for name, url in FILES.items():
            target = raw_dir / name
            if force or not target.exists():
                resp = client.get(url)
                resp.raise_for_status()
                target.write_bytes(resp.content)
            data = target.read_bytes()
            manifest[name] = {
                "url": url,
                "bytes": len(data),
                "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
                "fetched_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            }
    (raw_dir / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))
    return manifest

"""Build the POC dataset: scrape -> normalize -> annotate -> store -> BM25 gate.

Run: python -m toolprune.pipeline
Neatlogs spans are recorded locally; they export only when NEATLOGS_API_KEY is set.
"""

import json
import math
import os
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs

from toolprune import dataset, fetch

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
RAW_DIR = ROOT / "data" / "raw"
POC_DIR = ROOT / "data" / "poc"
DB_PATH = ROOT / "data" / "poc.sqlite"
GATE_TARGET = 31.68  # BM25 Recall@5 on LiveMCPBench, from the toolrank README (self-reported)
GATE_TOLERANCE = 2.0


def _tokens(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())


def bm25_recall_at_5(tools: list[dict], queries: list[dict], k1: float = 1.5, b: float = 0.75) -> float:
    docs = [_tokens(f"{t['name']} {t['name']} {t['description']} {t['server']}") for t in tools]
    avgdl = sum(len(d) for d in docs) / len(docs)
    df: Counter = Counter()
    for d in docs:
        df.update(set(d))
    n = len(docs)
    idf = {w: math.log(1 + (n - c + 0.5) / (c + 0.5)) for w, c in df.items()}
    tf_maps = [Counter(d) for d in docs]
    ids = [t["id"] for t in tools]

    scored_queries = [q for q in queries if q["gold_tools"]]
    total = 0.0
    for q in scored_queries:
        qtoks = set(_tokens(q["text"]))
        scores = []
        for i, tf in enumerate(tf_maps):
            dl = len(docs[i])
            s = 0.0
            for w in qtoks:
                if w in tf:
                    f = tf[w]
                    s += idf[w] * f * (k1 + 1) / (f + k1 * (1 - b + b * dl / avgdl))
            scores.append(s)
        top5 = {ids[i] for i in sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: -scores[i])[:5]}
        gold = set(q["gold_tools"])
        total += len(gold & top5) / len(gold)
    return 100.0 * total / len(scored_queries)


def main() -> None:
    neatlogs.init(
        workflow_name="tool-retrieval-eval",
        disable_export=not os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"),
    )

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-fetch")
    def scrape():
        return fetch.fetch_raw(RAW_DIR)

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-normalize")
    def normalize():
        tools = dataset.load_tools(RAW_DIR)
        queries = dataset.load_queries(RAW_DIR, tools)
        return tools, queries

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-enrich")
    def enrich(tools, queries):
        dataset.annotate_tools(tools)
        dataset.annotate_queries(queries, tools)
        return tools, queries

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-store")
    def persist(tools, queries):
        dataset.store(DB_PATH, POC_DIR, tools, queries)

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-gate-bm25")
    def gate(tools, queries):
        return bm25_recall_at_5(tools, queries)

    manifest = scrape()
    tools, queries = normalize()
    tools, queries = enrich(tools, queries)
    persist(tools, queries)
    recall5 = gate(tools, queries)

    (POC_DIR / "stats.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "servers": len({t["server"] for t in tools}),
        "tools": len(tools),
        "queries": len(queries),
        "queries_by_split": dict(Counter(q["split"] for q in queries)),
        "queries_by_type": dict(Counter(q["type"] for q in queries)),
        "queries_with_confusers": sum(q["collision"] for q in queries),
        "tools_by_effect": dict(Counter(t["effect"] for t in tools)),
        "unresolved_gold_names": sum(len(q["unresolved_gold"]) for q in queries),
        "ambiguous_gold_names": sum(len(q["ambiguous_gold"]) for q in queries),
        "bm25_recall_at_5": round(recall5, 2),
        "gate_target": GATE_TARGET,
        "gate_pass": abs(recall5 - GATE_TARGET) <= GATE_TOLERANCE,
        "sources": manifest,
    }, indent=2))
    neatlogs.flush()
    print(json.dumps(json.loads((POC_DIR / "stats.json").read_text()), indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Build the POC dataset: scrape -> normalize -> annotate -> store -> BM25 gate.

Run: python -m toolprune.pipeline
Neatlogs spans are recorded locally; they export only when NEATLOGS_API_KEY is set.
"""

import json
import math
import os
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs

from toolprune import dataset, fetch

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
RAW_DIR = ROOT / "data" / "raw"
POC_DIR = ROOT / "data" / "poc"
DB_PATH = ROOT / "data" / "poc.sqlite"
GATE_TARGET = 31.68  # BM25 Recall@5 on LiveMCPBench, from the toolrank README (self-reported)
GATE_TOLERANCE = 2.0


def _tokens(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())


def bm25_recall_at_5(tools: list[dict], queries: list[dict], k1: float = 1.5, b: float = 0.75) -> float:
    docs = [_tokens(f"{t['name']} {t['name']} {t['description']} {t['server']}") for t in tools]
    avgdl = sum(len(d) for d in docs) / len(docs)
    df: Counter = Counter()
    for d in docs:
        df.update(set(d))
    n = len(docs)
    idf = {w: math.log(1 + (n - c + 0.5) / (c + 0.5)) for w, c in df.items()}
    tf_maps = [Counter(d) for d in docs]
    ids = [t["id"] for t in tools]

    scored_queries = [q for q in queries if q["gold_tools"]]
    total = 0.0
    for q in scored_queries:
        qtoks = set(_tokens(q["text"]))
        scores = []
        for i, tf in enumerate(tf_maps):
            dl = len(docs[i])
            s = 0.0
            for w in qtoks:
                if w in tf:
                    f = tf[w]
                    s += idf[w] * f * (k1 + 1) / (f + k1 * (1 - b + b * dl / avgdl))
            scores.append(s)
        top5 = {ids[i] for i in sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: -scores[i])[:5]}
        gold = set(q["gold_tools"])
        total += len(gold & top5) / len(gold)
    return 100.0 * total / len(scored_queries)


def main() -> None:
    neatlogs.init(
        workflow_name="tool-retrieval-eval",
        disable_export=not os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"),
    )

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-fetch")
    def scrape():
        return fetch.fetch_raw(RAW_DIR)

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-normalize")
    def normalize():
        tools = dataset.load_tools(RAW_DIR)
        queries = dataset.load_queries(RAW_DIR, tools)
        return tools, queries

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-enrich")
    def enrich(tools, queries):
        dataset.annotate_tools(tools)
        dataset.annotate_queries(queries, tools)
        return tools, queries

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-store")
    def persist(tools, queries):
        dataset.store(DB_PATH, POC_DIR, tools, queries)

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-gate-bm25")
    def gate(tools, queries):
        return bm25_recall_at_5(tools, queries)

    manifest = scrape()
    tools, queries = normalize()
    tools, queries = enrich(tools, queries)
    persist(tools, queries)
    recall5 = gate(tools, queries)

    (POC_DIR / "stats.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "servers": len({t["server"] for t in tools}),
        "tools": len(tools),
        "queries": len(queries),
        "queries_by_split": dict(Counter(q["split"] for q in queries)),
        "queries_by_type": dict(Counter(q["type"] for q in queries)),
        "queries_with_confusers": sum(q["collision"] for q in queries),
        "tools_by_effect": dict(Counter(t["effect"] for t in tools)),
        "unresolved_gold_names": sum(len(q["unresolved_gold"]) for q in queries),
        "ambiguous_gold_names": sum(len(q["ambiguous_gold"]) for q in queries),
        "bm25_recall_at_5": round(recall5, 2),
        "gate_target": GATE_TARGET,
        "gate_pass": abs(recall5 - GATE_TARGET) <= GATE_TOLERANCE,
        "sources": manifest,
    }, indent=2))
    neatlogs.flush()
    print(json.dumps(json.loads((POC_DIR / "stats.json").read_text()), indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# ToolPrune

Hierarchical tool retrieval for MCP/API tools. An LLM enriches each tool with facet annotations. Queries route through the hierarchy (L0 function family, then L1 domain, then tool), so the agent sees only the few tools it needs.

Status: Phase 1, POC dataset and BM25 baseline. Hypothesis unproven. See `Idea_Draft.md` for the full plan.

## Agent design

- **Agent framework:** OpenAI Agents SDK (`openai-agents`).
- **Data contracts:** Pydantic models for every tool, query, annotation, and agent output. No untyped dicts cross a module boundary.
- **Structured output:** agent outputs are Pydantic models validated by the SDK.
- **Tracing:** neatlogs via its OpenAI Agents processor. Workflow names: `tool-retrieval-eval`, `tool-enrich`, `tool-route`.
- **Model calls:** temperature 0, cached by content hash, model name logged per call.

Pending: `Idea_Draft.md` says "plain code, no agent framework." This README follows the OpenAI Agents SDK decision. Update the draft once confirmed.

## Dataset (POC)

Source: LiveMCPBench (`ICIP/LiveMCPBench` on Hugging Face), scraped by `src/toolprune/fetch.py`. Provenance per file in `data/raw/manifest.json`.

| Item | Count |
| --- | --- |
| MCP servers | 70 |
| Tools | 527 |
| Queries (LiveMCPBench tasks) | 95 |
| Dev / test | 28 / 67 (seed 42) |

Stored in `data/poc.sqlite` plus JSONL under `data/poc/`. Build with:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m toolprune.pipeline
```

## Benchmark method

- **Baseline:** BM25 (k1=1.5, b=0.75) over tool name, description, and server name. Fully deterministic: fixed tokenization, sorted query terms, stable tie order, no randomness. Verified identical across hash seeds.
- **Metric:** Recall@5 per query = gold tools in top 5 / gold tools. Averaged over queries with at least one resolved gold tool.
- **Gate:** BM25 must reproduce about 31.7 Recall@5 (toolrank, self-reported) within 2 points before any other number is trusted. Current: 37.78, gate not passed.
- **Confusion rate:** gold tool missed in top 5 while a labeled confuser ranks in top 5. Definition fixed before the real run.

Labels are automatic. No human verification yet.

## Neatlogs setup (order)

1. Create a neatlogs API key. Store it as `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` in `.env` (gitignored). Never in code.
2. Confirm the pipeline exports: run `python -m toolprune.pipeline` with the key set, check spans in the neatlogs dashboard.
3. Wire the OpenAI Agents processor into the agent code once the agent exists.
4. Record a before/after trace pair for each change, with the numbers compared.
5. Record one failing run where an action fails and the agent recovers.

## Open questions

1. **Gold for ambiguous names.** 29 tool names exist on several servers (e.g. `search`, `fetch`, `read_file`). Resolve by hand, by server named in task steps, or drop?
2. **Unresolved gold.** 5 gold names are absent from the catalog (e.g. `ddg-search`, `get_maven_latest_version`). Missing from the snapshot, or renamed?
3. **Gate failure.** BM25 scores 37.78 vs 31.68. Doc-text mismatch with toolrank, or different query text? Which variant matches?
4. **Confusers.** Currently 0 queries have confusers because ambiguous names are excluded from gold. Count ambiguous candidates as confusers?
5. **Human verification.** Who checks queries and gold labels, and how many?
6. **Agent framework.** Confirm OpenAI Agents SDK over the plain-code plan in `Idea_Draft.md`.
7. **LLM for enrichment.** Which model, and which API key? None set in the environment yet.
8. **Collision subset.** Build the ~250-tool collision set from the plan, or use all 527?
9. **Neatlogs key.** Do you have one for this project?

4. **Store:** SQLite (`data/poc.sqlite`) and JSONL (`data/poc/`).

- Source: LiveMCPBench's human-written task annotations, not generated by us.

- Result: 65 queries are multi-tool, 30 are single-tool.

- It uses a real MCP tool universe, 70 servers, which is the setting the hypothesis is about.
- The queries are real tasks, not synthetic.
- Multi-tool tasks test the hierarchy's ability to return several tools.

"""Build the POC dataset: scrape -> normalize -> annotate -> store -> BM25 gate.

Run: python -m toolprune.pipeline
Neatlogs spans are recorded locally; they export only when NEATLOGS_API_KEY is set.
"""

import json
import math
import os
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs

from toolprune import dataset, fetch

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
RAW_DIR = ROOT / "data" / "raw"
POC_DIR = ROOT / "data" / "poc"
DB_PATH = ROOT / "data" / "poc.sqlite"
GATE_TARGET = 31.68  # BM25 Recall@5 on LiveMCPBench, from the toolrank README (self-reported)
GATE_TOLERANCE = 2.0


def _tokens(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())


def bm25_recall_at_5(tools: list[dict], queries: list[dict], k1: float = 1.5, b: float = 0.75) -> float:
    docs = [_tokens(f"{t['name']} {t['name']} {t['description']} {t['server']}") for t in tools]
    avgdl = sum(len(d) for d in docs) / len(docs)
    df: Counter = Counter()
    for d in docs:
        df.update(set(d))
    n = len(docs)
    idf = {w: math.log(1 + (n - c + 0.5) / (c + 0.5)) for w, c in df.items()}
    tf_maps = [Counter(d) for d in docs]
    ids = [t["id"] for t in tools]

    scored_queries = [q for q in queries if q["gold_tools"]]
    total = 0.0
    for q in scored_queries:
        qtoks = sorted(set(_tokens(q["text"])))  # fixed order: float sums must not depend on hash seed
        scores = []
        for i, tf in enumerate(tf_maps):
            dl = len(docs[i])
            s = 0.0
            for w in qtoks:
                if w in tf:
                    f = tf[w]
                    s += idf[w] * f * (k1 + 1) / (f + k1 * (1 - b + b * dl / avgdl))
            scores.append(s)
        top5 = {ids[i] for i in sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: -scores[i])[:5]}
        gold = set(q["gold_tools"])
        total += len(gold & top5) / len(gold)
    return 100.0 * total / len(scored_queries)


def main() -> None:
    neatlogs.init(
        workflow_name="tool-retrieval-eval",
        disable_export=not os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"),
    )

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-fetch")
    def scrape():
        return fetch.fetch_raw(RAW_DIR)

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-normalize")
    def normalize():
        tools = dataset.load_tools(RAW_DIR)
        queries = dataset.load_queries(RAW_DIR, tools)
        return tools, queries

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-enrich")
    def enrich(tools, queries):
        dataset.annotate_tools(tools)
        dataset.annotate_queries(queries, tools)
        return tools, queries

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-store")
    def persist(tools, queries):
        dataset.store(DB_PATH, POC_DIR, tools, queries)

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="tool-gate-bm25")
    def gate(tools, queries):
        return bm25_recall_at_5(tools, queries)

    manifest = scrape()
    tools, queries = normalize()
    tools, queries = enrich(tools, queries)
    persist(tools, queries)
    recall5 = gate(tools, queries)

    (POC_DIR / "stats.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "servers": len({t["server"] for t in tools}),
        "tools": len(tools),
        "queries": len(queries),
        "queries_by_split": dict(Counter(q["split"] for q in queries)),
        "queries_by_type": dict(Counter(q["type"] for q in queries)),
        "queries_with_confusers": sum(q["collision"] for q in queries),
        "tools_by_effect": dict(Counter(t["effect"] for t in tools)),
        "unresolved_gold_names": sum(len(q["unresolved_gold"]) for q in queries),
        "ambiguous_gold_names": sum(len(q["ambiguous_gold"]) for q in queries),
        "bm25_recall_at_5": round(recall5, 2),
        "gate_target": GATE_TARGET,
        "gate_pass": abs(recall5 - GATE_TARGET) <= GATE_TOLERANCE,
        "sources": manifest,
    }, indent=2))
    neatlogs.flush()
    print(json.dumps(json.loads((POC_DIR / "stats.json").read_text()), indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Scrape LiveMCPBench raw files from Hugging Face into data/raw and record a manifest."""

import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

BASE = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/ICIP/LiveMCPBench/resolve/main"
FILES = {
    "tools.json": f"{BASE}/tools/tools.json",
    "all_config.json": f"{BASE}/tools/all_config.json",
    "tasks.json": f"{BASE}/tasks/tasks.json",
}


def fetch_raw(raw_dir: Path, force: bool = False) -> dict:
    raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    manifest = {}
    with httpx.Client(follow_redirects=True, timeout=120) as client:
        for name, url in FILES.items():
            target = raw_dir / name
            if force or not target.exists():
                resp = client.get(url)
                resp.raise_for_status()
                target.write_bytes(resp.content)
            data = target.read_bytes()
            manifest[name] = {
                "url": url,
                "bytes": len(data),
                "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
                "fetched_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            }
    (raw_dir / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))
    return manifest

# ToolPrune

Hierarchical tool retrieval for MCP/API tools. An LLM enriches each tool with facet annotations. Queries route through the hierarchy (L0 function family, then L1 domain, then tool), so the agent sees only the few tools it needs.

Status: Phase 1, POC dataset and BM25 baseline. Hypothesis unproven. See `Idea_Draft.md` for the full plan.

## Agent design

- **Agent framework:** OpenAI Agents SDK (`openai-agents`).
- **Data contracts:** Pydantic models for every tool, query, annotation, and agent output. No untyped dicts cross a module boundary.
- **Structured output:** agent outputs are Pydantic models validated by the SDK.
- **Tracing:** neatlogs via its OpenAI Agents processor. Workflow names: `tool-retrieval-eval`, `tool-enrich`, `tool-route`.
- **Model calls:** temperature 0, cached by content hash, model name logged per call.

Pending: `Idea_Draft.md` says "plain code, no agent framework." This README follows the OpenAI Agents SDK decision. Update the draft once confirmed.

## Dataset (POC)

Source: LiveMCPBench (`ICIP/LiveMCPBench` on Hugging Face), scraped by `src/toolprune/fetch.py`. Provenance per file in `data/raw/manifest.json`.

| Item | Count |
| --- | --- |
| MCP servers | 70 |
| Tools | 527 |
| Queries (LiveMCPBench tasks) | 95 |
| Dev / test | 28 / 67 (seed 42) |

Stored in `data/poc.sqlite` plus JSONL under `data/poc/`. Build with:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m toolprune.pipeline
```

## Benchmark method

- **Baseline:** BM25 (k1=1.5, b=0.75) over tool name, description, and server name. Fully deterministic: fixed tokenization, sorted query terms, stable tie order, no randomness. Verified identical across hash seeds.
- **Metric:** Recall@5 per query = gold tools in top 5 / gold tools. Averaged over queries with at least one resolved gold tool.
- **Gate:** BM25 must reproduce about 31.7 Recall@5 (toolrank, self-reported) within 2 points before any other number is trusted. Current: 37.78, gate not passed.
- **Confusion rate:** gold tool missed in top 5 while a labeled confuser ranks in top 5. Definition fixed before the real run.

Labels are automatic. No human verification yet.

## Neatlogs setup (order)

1. Create a neatlogs API key. Store it as `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` in `.env` (gitignored). Never in code.
2. Confirm the pipeline exports: run `python -m toolprune.pipeline` with the key set, check spans in the neatlogs dashboard.
3. Wire the OpenAI Agents processor into the agent code once the agent exists.
4. Record a before/after trace pair for each change, with the numbers compared.
5. Record one failing run where an action fails and the agent recovers.

## Open questions

1. **Gold for ambiguous names.** 29 tool names exist on several servers (e.g. `search`, `fetch`, `read_file`). Resolve by hand, by server named in task steps, or drop?
2. **Unresolved gold.** 5 gold names are absent from the catalog (e.g. `ddg-search`, `get_maven_latest_version`). Missing from the snapshot, or renamed?
3. **Gate failure.** BM25 scores 37.78 vs 31.68. Doc-text mismatch with toolrank, or different query text? Which variant matches?
4. **Confusers.** Currently 0 queries have confusers because ambiguous names are excluded from gold. Count ambiguous candidates as confusers?
5. **Human verification.** Who checks queries and gold labels, and how many?
6. **Agent framework.** Confirm OpenAI Agents SDK over the plain-code plan in `Idea_Draft.md`.
7. **LLM for enrichment.** Which model, and which API key? None set in the environment yet.
8. **Collision subset.** Build the ~250-tool collision set from the plan, or use all 527?
9. **Neatlogs key.** Do you have one for this project?

content.text:
The dataset is back to the state you get from downloading. Derived files are deleted and nothing is normalized or annotated.

**What's on disk**

`data/raw/`, unmodified, hashes verified against the manifest:

| File | Bytes | Records |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tools/tools.json` | 1,133,864 | 70 servers, 527 tools |
| `tasks/tasks.json` | 82,022 | 95 tasks |
| `tools/all_config.json` | 47,183 | 70 server configs (not used yet) |
| `manifest.json` | 830 | URL, size, sha256, fetch time per file |

**Raw record shapes**

- **Server entry** (`tools.json`): `name`, `category`, `web`, `config`, `description`, `organization`, and `tools`. `tools` is keyed by server name.
- **Tool** (inside a server): `name`, `description`, `inputSchema`, `annotations`.
- **Task** (`tasks.json`): `task_id`, `Question`, `answers`, `category`, `file_name`, `Annotator Metadata` (`Steps`, `Tools`, `Number of tools`).

Example from the raw file: server `Bing_CN_MCP` (key `bing-cn-mcp`, category Discovery) has tool `bing_search`, input `query` (required) and `num_results`. The first task asks for a PDF report with a word cloud, with gold tools listed as text in `Annotator Metadata.Tools`.

**Code changes**

- `src/toolprune/dataset.py` deleted. It held normalization, gold matching, confusers, and splits.
- `src/toolprune/pipeline.py` now only fetches. It no longer runs BM25 or writes derived outputs.
- `src/toolprune/fetch.py`: fixed a provenance bug. Re-running used to stamp a new `fetched_at` on files that were not re-downloaded. Now it keeps the original time unless a file is actually fetched.
- `README.md`: the dataset section describes the raw files. The benchmark section still describes the BM25 gate (37.78 vs 31.68). That text is now stale, and I'll rewrite it when adaptation starts.

Ready for the adaptation step. Tell me which first: normalization into a schema, or the gold-resolution rules.
